description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for universal technical action classes used by A.R.I.A. during diagnosis, inspection, measurement, testing, verification, validation, correction, monitoring, and escalation. This Registry defines what kind of technical operation an action represents. It does not define manufacturer-specific, product-specific, technology-specific, or procedure-specific actions.

principles: An action class describes the generic technical nature of an operation.
A runtime action instance is identified by act_<UUID>.
A Registry action class is not a runtime action identifier.
Technology-specific and manufacturer-specific procedures shall reference an applicable universal action class rather than becoming universal Core action classes.
An action may produce evidence, outcomes, measurements, configuration changes, validation results, or other technical state changes.
Action completion and action success are distinct.
An action may be diagnostically useful even when it does not correct the underlying condition.
An action may be operationally successful while providing little diagnostic information.
Action selection is owned by Decision and Routing behavior, not by this Registry.
Safety, authorization, access, service impact, reversibility, and technical prerequisites may constrain execution.
Repeated equivalent actions require technical justification when valid evidence already exists.
A.R.I.A. shall preserve the distinction between requesting an action, executing an action, and evaluating the action result.

categories.description: Actions whose primary purpose is obtaining technical information.
Actions that directly observe technical or physical state.
Actions that obtain quantitative technical measurements.
Actions that compare, calculate, correlate, or otherwise analyze technical information.
Controlled actions intended to discriminate, isolate, reproduce, or validate technical conditions.
Actions that determine whether technical state conforms to an expected or required condition.
Actions intended to modify technical state to correct or mitigate a condition.
Actions intended to establish whether defined technical acceptance or resolution criteria are satisfied.
Actions involving observation across time or deliberate waiting for a technically meaningful interval.
Actions transferring technical handling when current authority, expertise, capability, access, or safety limits are insufficient.

action_types.description: Directly observe a physical, logical, operational, environmental, or technical condition without intentionally modifying it.
Obtain existing technical information from a system, source, artifact, database, interface, device, document, or repository without materially changing the subject system.

Perform a deliberate technical inspection of physical or logical state to identify defects, inconsistencies, installation conditions, connectivity, orientation, damage, contamination, or other relevant conditions.
Obtain a quantitative technical value using an instrument, system, sensor, tester, measurement process, or defined measurement method.
Compare two or more technically relevant values, states, systems, components, configurations, periods, sources, or reference conditions.
Produce a deterministic technical result from defined inputs using an identified calculation, formula, conversion, algorithm, or engineering method.
Evaluate temporal, contextual, behavioral, or technical relationships among multiple evidence items or system conditions without asserting causality solely from correlation.
rules: Correlation shall not be represented as causal proof without additional support.

action_types.description: Perform a controlled technical procedure intended to evaluate behavior, establish a condition, challenge a hypothesis, or produce discriminating evidence.
Perform a controlled operation intended to separate a component, path, variable, configuration, interface, endpoint, environment, or failure domain from competing explanations.
rules: Isolation actions should identify which variables are intentionally changed or held constant.
Uncontrolled simultaneous changes reduce diagnostic value.

action_types.description: Determine whether a technical state, value, configuration, installation, relationship, compatibility condition, or requirement matches an expected or authoritative reference.
Perform or evaluate a defined technical validation intended to establish whether explicit acceptance, recovery, correction, diagnosis, or resolution criteria are satisfied.
rules: Validation success does not automatically prove exact causal mechanism.
Validation criteria shall be explicit when technically material.

action_types.description: Create, modify, apply, or restore technical configuration intended to establish a desired technical state.
rules: Configuration actions may require rollback information.
Expected and actual resulting configuration should remain distinguishable.

action_types.description: Physically or logically adjust an existing technical element to improve alignment, calibration, tuning, positioning, level, timing, or other operating condition.
Restore a defective technical component, connection, assembly, structure, circuit, interface, or installation without replacing the entire target object.
Remove an existing technical component, assembly, device, module, cable, interface, or other object and install a substitute.
Disconnect and reconnect, remove and reinstall, or otherwise reseat a component or connection while preserving its intended identity and function.
Restart, reboot, reload, reset, power-cycle, or otherwise reinitialize a technical system or component.
rules: Restart may restore operation without identifying root cause.
Restart shall not be treated as causal proof.

action_types.description: Enable, activate, bring into service, or restore an existing technical function, interface, feature, path, component, or configuration state.
Disable, deactivate, remove from service, or administratively suppress a technical function, interface, feature, path, component, or configuration state.
Restore a previously known or explicitly recorded technical state after a change, test, deployment, adjustment, or configuration operation.
rules: The rollback target state should be explicitly identified.
Rollback itself does not establish that the prior state was technically correct.

action_types.description: Observe a technical condition repeatedly or continuously across a defined interval to assess recurrence, stability, intermittency, degradation, recovery, or temporal behavior.
Deliberately allow a technically meaningful interval or external dependency to elapse before reassessment.
rules: WAIT is a technical action only when the passage of time or an expected external dependency has diagnostic or validation value.
WAIT shall not be used merely to represent case lifecycle WAITING.

action_types.description: Transfer or elevate technical handling because current authority, expertise, access, capability, safety boundary, manufacturer support requirement, or engineering scope is insufficient.
rules: Escalation is a valid technical action and not necessarily a diagnostic failure.
Case lifecycle ESCALATED remains a separate state semantic.

action_class_rules.rule: The Registry shall define universal action classes rather than product-specific or technology-specific procedures.
A runtime action instance shall use act_<UUID> identity.
Technology-specific procedures shall reference one applicable Core action class.
A specific technical procedure may include multiple ordered Core action classes when the procedure legitimately contains multiple operations.
Action classification shall describe what operation is performed, not why the action was selected.
Why an action was selected belongs to Decision and Routing reasoning.
Action completion shall remain distinct from successful technical outcome.
Corrective action success shall remain distinct from causal proof.
A successful action may generate evidence supporting a hypothesis without independently confirming exclusivity of cause.
An unsuccessful action may still produce diagnostically useful evidence.
An action may be prevented from execution by safety, authorization, access, operational, service-impact, prerequisite, or tooling constraints.
Equivalent completed actions should not be repeated without a material technical justification.
A material state change, poor-quality prior execution, insufficient evidence quality, or changed technical scope may justify repetition.
Action risk and action invasiveness shall be evaluated independently from action class.
Action reversibility shall be evaluated independently from action class.
Action class shall not encode hypothesis probability, evidence confidence, diagnostic confidence, or route utility.
Action class shall not encode case lifecycle status or reasoning state.
The same Core action class may apply across multiple technical domains.
Manufacturer-specific action names remain domain knowledge and shall not be added to Core merely because they are frequently used.

Action instructions, expected evidence, prerequisites, compatible products, required tools, safety requirements, and execution methods belong to runtime action records or domain procedure knowledge rather than the Core action-class vocabulary.

risk_semantics.principle: Risk is evaluated for an action instance or procedure, not inferred solely from action class.
rules: The same action class may carry different risk in different contexts.
A measurement may be passive in one system and hazardous in another.
A restart may be low-impact in a lab system and high-impact in a live production system.
Safety constraints may prohibit execution regardless of diagnostic utility.
Reversibility is an action-instance or procedure characteristic.
Reversible diagnostic experiments may be preferred when they provide comparable information value.
Irreversible actions require stronger justification and applicable authorization.
Original state required for rollback should be preserved when technically practical.
Execution status is not lifecycle status.
COMPLETED means execution ended; it does not mean the technical objective was achieved.
FAILED describes execution failure and does not necessarily mean the diagnostic hypothesis was false.
BLOCKED requires preservation of the blocking condition.
SKIPPED should preserve the reason an otherwise relevant action was not performed.

domain_mapping_examples.description: A microwave-domain procedure for obtaining received signal level.
A microwave-domain engineering calculation and verification procedure.
A product or technology-domain version verification procedure.

decision_engine: generates and scores candidate runtime actions
evaluates cost, time, safety, service impact, user effort, reversibility, and expected utility
routing_engine: selects and records route progression from eligible candidate actions
applies routing dependencies and repetition penalties
records why an action was selected or bypassed
registry: defines the universal technical action class

technical_corpus_boundary.principle: Specific technical procedures belong to technical knowledge rather than the universal Core action vocabulary.
rules: Domain procedure knowledge may reference Core action classes.
Domain procedure knowledge may define expected evidence, measurements, tools, prerequisites, hazards, context requirements, and expected outcomes.
Domain procedures shall not redefine Core action semantics.

prohibited_uses: Using ACT-RF-* or similar technology-specific procedure codes as universal Core action classes.
Using Registry action class names as runtime action identifiers.
Treating action completion as successful correction.
Treating successful correction as automatic causal proof.
Using action class to encode probability.
Using action class to encode confidence.
Using action class to encode route utility.
Using action class to encode case lifecycle status.
Using action class to encode reasoning state.
Using WAIT as a substitute for lifecycle WAITING.
Using ESCALATE as a substitute for lifecycle ESCALATED.
Allowing product-specific procedures to expand the Core Registry without a genuinely universal semantic need.
Repeating semantically equivalent actions merely because they use different wording.
Allowing action risk to be inferred solely from the generic action class.
Allowing action reversibility to be inferred solely from the generic action class.
